note.note:
History:
- 26-yo woman reports progressive anxiety for ~2 months, temporally related to starting a new, stressful job in fashion retail head office.
- Main features: daily morning dread of leaving the house for work; palpitations on awakening (subjectively irregular, lasting 2–10 min, no true chest pain); severe insomnia (bed 22:00–23:00, sleep latency prolonged, total sleep ~3–4 h, shallow); early awakening with racing heart; daytime fatigue, low energy, anhedonia, social withdrawal, cessation of running/tennis.
- Mood: feels “down” most of the time including weekends; no suicidal ideation, no prior depressive episodes.
- Anxiety triggers: thoughts of work performance, hostile supervisor, fear of being late; crowded public transport also stressful.
- No previous similar anxiety, no full panic attacks, no avoidance severe enough to miss work (though frequently contemplates calling in sick).
- Diet: unchanged except increased chocolate; weight change not reported.
- Alcohol: binge drinking most Fridays/Saturdays (“over limit”) plus occasional weekday wine with parents.
- Tobacco: occasional smoker; no recreational drugs.
- Family history: mother with past depression.
- Lives with parents; good family support.

Past Medical History:
- Chronic illnesses: none disclosed.
- Surgeries/hospitalizations: not mentioned.
- Allergies: not recorded.
- Medications: none reported.

Physical Examination:
- Tele-consultation; no formal exam performed.
- Reported: palpitations without syncope; no chest pain apart from discomfort during rapid heartbeat; alert, oriented.
- Other findings: Not recorded.

Impression:
- Adjustment-related anxiety disorder (early Generalized Anxiety Disorder) with secondary insomnia and work-related stress.
  • Major depressive episode (subthreshold) and medical causes of palpitations (e.g., thyroid disorder, anaemia, arrhythmia) considered but less likely at present and will be screened with blood tests.

Management Plan:
- Provide link for NHS self-referral to talking therapy (CBT-based service); patient agreeable.
- Email/attach online self-help resources for anxiety and sleep hygiene.
- Order basic screening bloods (FBC, TFTs, electrolytes, glucose, iron studies) to exclude physiological contributors to palpitations/anxiety.
- Advise patient to phone support line to arrange phlebotomy; schedule GP follow-up one week after results available.
- Safety-net: return earlier if anxiety escalates, function deteriorates, or new red-flag symptoms (chest pain, syncope, suicidal thoughts) occur.
- Discussed that medication (e.g., SSRIs or short-term anxiolytics) could be considered later if non-pharmacologic measures insufficient.

Patient Summary:
Ms Valerie Cole presents with a 2-month history of work-triggered anxiety, insomnia, and palpitations. Clinical picture most consistent with adjustment-related anxiety; will begin CBT-based therapy and have baseline labs to rule out medical precipitants.

Key Takeaways:
- Self-refer to talking therapy via link provided and begin online CBT resources immediately.
- Implement sleep-hygiene measures and monitor caffeine/alcohol intake.
- Arrange and attend blood tests; book follow-up to review results and progress.

Next Steps:
- Complete ordered blood work within the next week.
- GP follow-up appointment (tele- or in-person) after labs.
- Consider pharmacotherapy if symptoms persist or worsen despite therapy.
